events.title: Battle of Bosworth Field
events.description: Richard III of England was killed in battle against Henry Tudor, Earl of Richmond, near Market Bosworth in Leicestershire. Henry was subsequently crowned Henry VII.
events.significance: The battle ended the Plantagenet dynasty and the Wars of the Roses, establishing the Tudor dynasty that ruled England until 1603.

events.title: First Geneva Convention Signed
events.description: Twelve European nations signed the first Geneva Convention in Geneva, Switzerland, establishing rules for the humane treatment of wounded soldiers on the battlefield and the neutrality of medical personnel.
events.significance: It laid the foundation of modern international humanitarian law and led to the establishment of the International Committee of the Red Cross as a recognized protector of war victims.

events.title: First Car Ride by a U.S. President
events.description: Theodore Roosevelt became the first sitting U.S. president to ride in an automobile, when he traveled in a Columbia Electric Victoria in Hartford, Connecticut.
events.significance: The event symbolized the arrival of the automobile age and the growing acceptance of motor vehicles in American public life.

events.title: Death of Michael Collins
events.description: Irish revolutionary leader Michael Collins was killed in an ambush at Béal na Bláth, County Cork, during the Irish Civil War. He was 31 years old.
events.significance: Collins was a key figure in the Irish War of Independence and the negotiation of the Anglo-Irish Treaty; his death was a major blow to the new Irish Free State.

events.title: Huey Newton Killed
events.description: Huey P. Newton, co-founder of the Black Panther Party, was shot and killed in Oakland, California.
events.significance: Newton was a leading figure in the Black Power movement of the 1960s and 1970s, and his death marked the end of an influential, controversial era in American civil rights history.
